title: Quantifying _in vivo_ recruitment of naïve CTL towards individual dendritic cells by standard immunofluorescence histology
protocol: Isolate spleens from CTL-donor mice.
Generate a single cell suspension by extruding the spleen through a steel sieve with the plunger of a 2 ml syringe and filtering through a Nylon sieve (100 µm).
Centrifuge cell suspension at 300 g for 6 minutes, 4°C.
Resuspend cells in 600 μl of MACS buffer.
Add 20 μl of alpha murine CD8 MicroBeads per spleen and incubate for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Centrifuge at 300 g for 6 minutes, 4°C.
Embed MACS columns (1 column per 2-3 spleens) in magnetic field and equilibrate with 3 ml of MACS buffer.
Resuspend cells in 3 ml of cold MACS buffer.
Pipette filtered cell suspension on column.
Wash the column with 3 ml MACS buffer.
Remove MACS columns from magnetic field.
Rinse the columns with 4 ml MACS buffer.
Capture passage (positive fraction of cells) in a 15 ml tube.
Centrifuge at 300 g for 6 minutes, 4°C.
Resuspend cells in 5 ml of PBS in a 15 ml tube.
Add 2.5 μl of FarRed staining solution into the lid of the tube.
Invert the tube carefully and incubate for 20 minutes at 37°C.
Stop staining reaction by adding 7 ml of ice-cold PBS and centrifuge at 300 g for 6 minutes, 4°C.
Resuspend cells in PBS.
Adjust the cell number to 12.5 x 10^6 cells per ml of PBS.
Inject 200 μl (2.5 x 10^6 cells) intravenously into mice of favored genetic background.
Inject antigen with or without adjuvant intravenously into mice 16 hours after adoptive T cell transfer.
Isolate spleens from injected mice after 10 hours.
Rinse isolated spleens briefly in ice-cold PBS.
Embed rinsed spleens directly in Tissue-Tek®.
Store tissue blocks at -20°C overnight.
Prepare 5 μm cryosections from frozen tissue blocks using a microtome/cryostat at -18°C.
Discard at least two sections between individual slides to avoid staining the same cells on different sections.
Transfer cryosections onto microscope slides for further treatment.
Dry sections for several hours.
Fix sections with iced acetone for 10 minutes, then air-dry them for some time.
Apply blocking solution (1% BSA in PBS) to samples for 1 hour at room temperature.
Stain sections with alpha murine B220-PE antibody for 1 hour at room temperature, then wash twice with PBS.
Cover stained sections with mounting medium (Immu-Mount).
Cover slides.
Store tissue slices at room temperature for up to one week.
View sections under a fluorescence microscope.
Capture images of the sections.
Determine the number of labeled cells using appropriate software.
Use an Olympus IX71 with a 10x objective.
Count T cell numbers utilizing "Touch count" mode.
Analyze areas using "Closed polygon" mode in Cell F software.
